## Declarations and implementations

```plato

    //==
    // # The derived Integer surface
    //
    // Reference bodies for every `Integer` member that used to be a host intrinsic
    // but is a formula over the surviving kernel (plato-378): the six arithmetic
    // operators, `LessThanOrEquals` / `Equals` / `Hash`, the six bitwise
    // operations, `MinValue` / `MaxValue` and `ToNumber`.
    //
    // As in the Number section above, bodies use only the intrinsic
    // relations (`<=`, `==`), and the relational family (LessThan, GreaterThan,
    // GreaterThanOrEquals, Compare, Clamp, Lesser, Greater) is absent because
    // `core.library.plato` already provides it generically over
    // IOrderable.

    //==
    // # Sign and magnitude

    // The absolute value. Precondition: self is not MinValue, whose magnitude
    // is not representable.
    Abs(self: Integer): Integer
        => 0 <= self ? self : -self;

    // -1, 0 or 1 according to the sign.
    Sign(self: Integer): Integer
        => 0 <= self ? (self <= 0 ? 0 : 1) : -1;

    // The lesser of two integers.
    Min(a: Integer, b: Integer): Integer
        => a <= b ? a : b;

    // The greater of two integers.
    Max(a: Integer, b: Integer): Integer
        => a <= b ? b : a;

    //==
    // # Constants
    //
    // Dispatch on an ignored receiver, the tree's constant idiom.

    // The additive identity.
    Zero(_: Integer): Integer
        => 0;

    // The multiplicative identity.
    One(_: Integer): Integer
        => 1;

    //==
    // # Enumeration

    // The integers 0 up to but excluding self, in order: the standard index
    // range behind every count-driven traversal. Reads as `n.Range`.
    Range(self: Integer): Array<Integer>
        => MapRange(self, i => i);

    //==
    // # The derived Number surface
    //
    // Reference bodies for every `Number` member that used to be a host intrinsic
    // but is a formula over the surviving kernel (plato-378). The kernel is the
    // six arithmetic operators, `LessThanOrEquals` / `Equals` / `Hash`, `Floor`,
    // `Round`, `Sqrt` / `Exp` / `NaturalLog` / `Pow` / `FusedMultiplyAdd`,
    // `Sin` / `Cos` / `Atan2Radians`, the four limits, `IsNaN` / `IsInfinite` and
    // `ToInteger`.
    //
    // Bodies are written against the INTRINSIC relations only (`<=`, `==`), never
    // against the derived `<` or `>`, so nothing here can recurse back through the
    // IOrderable generics in `core.library.plato`.
    //
    // Accuracy note: a native `Log10`, `Cbrt` or `Acos` is usually a few ulp better
    // than the identity below. That is the whole point of the plato-368 override
    // table — these bodies fix the SEMANTICS and a backend substitutes its own
    // verified implementation. Do not tighten a formula here to chase ulps.
    //
    // The relational family (LessThan, GreaterThan, GreaterThanOrEquals, Compare,
    // Clamp, Lesser, Greater, Min3, Max3) is deliberately absent: those are already
    // generic over IOrderable in `core.library.plato`, and LIBRARIES.md
    // ground rule 11 forbids a per-type copy.

    //==
    // # Sign and magnitude

    // The absolute value: distance from zero.
    Abs(self: Number): Number
        => 0.0 <= self ? self : -self;

    // -1, 0 or 1 according to the sign. Zero is unsigned: both -0.0 and 0.0
    // report 0.
    Sign(self: Number): Integer
        => 0.0 <= self ? (self <= 0.0 ? 0 : 1) : -1;

    // The magnitude of self carrying the sign of y. A y of -0.0 reads as
    // non-negative here, where IEEE copysign reads it as negative.
    CopySign(self: Number, y: Number): Number
        => 0.0 <= y ? self.Abs : -self.Abs;

    // The lesser of two numbers.
    Min(self: Number, other: Number): Number
        => self <= other ? self : other;

    // The greater of two numbers.
    Max(self: Number, other: Number): Number
        => self <= other ? other : self;

    //==
    // # Powers and roots

    // The number multiplied by itself.
    Square(self: Number): Number
        => self * self;

    // One over the number. Division by zero yields an infinity rather than
    // signalling, as everywhere in this vocabulary. Synonym of `Inverse`.
    Reciprocal(self: Number): Number
        => 1.0 / self;

    // The real cube root, defined for negative input by odd symmetry —
    // Pow alone would return NaN there.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cube_root)
    Cbrt(self: Number): Number
        => 0.0 <= self ? self.Pow(1.0 / 3.0) : -((-self).Pow(1.0 / 3.0));

    //==
    // # Rounding
    //
    // Floor is the kernel; the other two are its reflections.

    // The smallest whole value greater than or equal to self.
    Ceiling(self: Number): Number
        => -((-self).Floor);

    // The whole part, rounding toward zero.
    Truncate(self: Number): Number
        => 0.0 <= self ? self.Floor : self.Ceiling;

    //==
    // # Logarithms
    //
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logarithm)

    // The logarithm of self in the given base.
    Log(self: Number, newBase: Number): Number
        => self.NaturalLog / newBase.NaturalLog;

    // The base-two logarithm.
    Log2(self: Number): Number
        => self.NaturalLog / Number.Ln2;

    // The base-ten logarithm.
    Log10(self: Number): Number
        => self.NaturalLog / Number.Ln10;
```
